verses.text: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham on his way back from defeating the kings and blessed him.
Abraham gave him a tenth of everything. His name means ‘king of righteousness,’ and he was also king of Salem, meaning ‘king of peace.’
He has no recorded father or mother or family line, no beginning of life or end of days. Like the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.
Think about how great he was: even Abraham the patriarch gave him a tenth of the best part of the plunder.
The descendants of Levi who become priests are commanded by the law to collect a tenth from the people—their own relatives, even though they too are descended from Abraham.
But Melchizedek, who wasn't descended from Levi, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed the one who had received God's promises.
No one disputes that the greater person blesses the lesser.
In one case, people who die collect a tenth; in the other, Scripture testifies that the one who received it lives on.
We could even say that Levi, who collects tithes, paid a tithe through Abraham,
because Levi was still in his ancestor's body when Melchizedek met Abraham.
If the Levitical priesthood could bring perfection (and under it the people received the law), why was another priest needed, one in the order of Melchizedek instead of Aaron?
When the priesthood changes, the law must change too.
The one these things are said about belonged to a different tribe, and no one from that tribe ever served at the altar.
It's clear that our Lord came from Judah, a tribe Moses never connected with priesthood.
This becomes even clearer when another priest like Melchizedek appears,
one who became a priest not through a law about physical ancestry, but through the power of an indestructible life.
Scripture testifies, ‘You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.’
The earlier command is set aside because it was weak and ineffective
(the law made nothing perfect). A better hope has now been introduced, and through it we draw near to God.
Jesus didn't become a priest without an oath.

The others became priests without an oath, but Jesus became a priest with an oath from the one who said, ‘The Lord has sworn and won't change his mind: You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.’
Because of this oath, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.
There have been many priests, because death kept them from continuing in office.
But Jesus lives forever, so his priesthood never passes to anyone else.
That's why he can save completely those who come to God through him. He always lives to speak to God on their behalf.
We need just this kind of high priest: holy, innocent, pure, set apart from sinners, and raised above the heavens.
He doesn't need to offer sacrifices every day like other high priests—first for his own sins and then for the people's. He did this once for all when he offered himself.
The law appoints weak men as high priests, but the oath, which came after the law, appoints the Son, who has been made perfect forever.
